instruction.text: Match each punctuation mark to its name.
Select all parts of the independent clause below.

hint.text:
Independent clauses can stand alone as a sentence.

For example:
Liam is tired because he woke up early.
The school (outside town) is huge.

feedback.finish: When dashes, brackets or commas are inserted in the middle of the sentence, additional information is added to the sentence. In this case, information is added to the subject of the sentence, the bakery.

instruction.text: Select all parts of the independent clause below.

feedback.finish: The information within the punctuation is additional, not essential. In this example, we would not need to use the commas if the information were essential.

instruction.text: Select all parts of the independent clause below.
Select the sentence in which the punctuation is used correctly.

b: ++In Ghana, a country on the coast of West Africa, more than 80 languages are spoken.
In Ghana a country on the coast of West Africa more than, 80 languages, are spoken.

feedback.end: Commas are the most common punctuation used to set aside information. In this example, more information is added to the subject, Ghana.

b: ++Almost everyone in the family (the only exception being Georgia) is vegetarian.
Almost everyone, (in the family the only exception being Georgia) is vegetarian.
atoms.sound: Almost everyone in the family, (the only exception being Georgia), is vegetarian

feedback.end: Brackets are used to set aside information in a very visible way.

b: The hotel that’s owned by my uncle — has a great view of — the city.
++The hotel — that’s owned by my uncle — has a great view of the city.

feedback.end: Dashes are also used to more visibly set information aside, but are slightly less dramatic than brackets.

b: ++Frida and Rachel, who've been friends for over ten years, love to play video games.
Frida and Rachel, who've been friends, for over ten years, love to play video games.
The festival which is celebrated — every year in — April is always fantastic.
++The festival — which is celebrated every year in April — is always fantastic.
Layla my older cousin prefers cycling, to, driving a car.
++Layla, my older cousin, prefers cycling to driving a car.
